value.rationale: The nonlinear advection is the defining nonlocal coupling of Lorenz–96 and is exactly the quantity that reduced models and data-driven closures must represent. Despite depending quadratically on neighboring sites, its stationary conditional mean given the local state is forced to be the simple affine law \(x_i-F\) for every compact invariant regime. The theorem also identifies the entire unexplained conditional variance with coordinate-acceleration energy and converts that into an exact site-time activity gap. This supplies a natural, parameter-exact benchmark for closure, regression, data-assimilation, and surrogate-model statistics in one of the standard high-dimensional chaotic test systems.
